editorial:
Imagine living in a perfect little town back in 1958 where every lawn is green and everyone seems happy. That is the world you enter before things go completely wrong. You follow two young sisters who lose their parents and move in with their Aunt Ruth. At first, it seems like a normal family move, but you quickly realize that Ruth is not a normal aunt. She has a scary way of disciplining children that turns into something way worse. You see the story through the eyes of a 12-year-old boy next door who becomes friends with the girls and realizes they are in serious danger. The vibe starts off sunny but quickly turns into a nightmare that makes you feel uneasy.

The acting is what really makes this work because the actress playing Ruth is genuinely terrifying. You will hate her and fear for the kids in every scene. The pacing is steady, though some parts are very hard to watch because the abuse is so realistic. If you like dark stories that show the scary side of humans, you will find this gripping. It is a heavy ride, but the payoff is worth it.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the neighborhood kids and the boy try to save the sisters. In a final act of madness, Ruth's control slips and the violence peaks. The sisters are eventually rescued, but the trauma stays with them. The boy who helped them is forever changed by the horror he witnessed. It ends with a sad feeling, showing that while the villain is stopped, the damage to the children cannot be easily fixed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark crime dramas and psychological thrillers.
